title: DWCP v3 test-suite debt: aspirational APIs, synthetic benchmarks/, real test failures (found unblocking novacron-38p)
description:
## Overview

Discovered while unblocking novacron-38p (Phase 0 DWCP benchmarks). Root cause of the blocker: `backend/core/network/dwcp/v3/tests/go.mod` and `backend/core/network/dwcp/v3/benchmarks/go.mod` were stray nested Go modules (bare, no meaningful requires) that walled those two directories off from the parent `backend/core` module. This meant `go build`/`go vet`/`go test` never ran against either directory — not from CI, not from any developer's `go test ./...`. Every bug documented below was invisible until the module boundary was removed this session. None of this is new breakage; it's debt that predates this session and was simply never compiled.

Both stray `go.mod` files have been deleted (git-tracked deletion) so `v3/tests` and `v3/benchmarks` are now ordinary packages in the `backend/core` module. `backend/core/go.mod` needed one surgical addition: `github.com/golang/snappy v1.0.0` (already present in `go.sum` as an indirect dep at the matching version, promoted to direct; diff is a single added line, no `go mod tidy` was run — a first attempt at `go mod tidy` pruned 2277 unrelated lines and was reverted).

## v3/benchmarks — fully synthetic, not real measurements

`backend/core/network/dwcp/v3/benchmarks/*.go` has **zero imports of the `dwcp` package** (verified via grep). Every "benchmark" there (`AMSTTransportThroughput`, `AMSTZeroCopyTransfer`, `ASSRaftConsensusLatency`, `ACPPBFTConsensusThroughput`, etc.) is a closed-form formula over hardcoded scenario tables — it benchmarks the test's own arithmetic, not the DWCP implementation. Numbers like "38568 GB/s zero-copy throughput" are not measurements of anything real. This package now compiles and runs cleanly, but **its output must not be used as evidence of DWCP v3 performance** for the Go/No-Go decision. Recommend either deleting this package or clearly marking it as a simulation/design-target scaffold, not a benchmark suite.

## v3/tests — real benchmarks (compile-fixed, now passing) vs. real bugs (found along the way)

### Compile-time bugs fixed this session (mechanical, all pre-existing, all verified individually before touching)
- Dozens of dead `ctx := context.Background()` declarations across `amst_v3_test.go`, `backward_compat_test.go`, `disaster_recovery_test.go`, `integration_test.go`, `mode_switching_test.go`, `phase4_final_validation_test.go`, `regression_test.go` — each verified via full-function grep to have zero other references before removal.
- Unused imports removed after individually confirming zero usage: `context`, `crypto/rand`, `math/big`, `github.com/stretchr/testify/require` — scattered across `amst_v3_test.go`, `disaster_recovery_test.go`, `mode_switching_test.go`, `phase4_final_validation_test.go`, `phase5_production_validation_test.go`, `production_validation_test.go`, `regression_test.go`.
- Duplicate `func min(a, b int) int` (redundant with the Go 1.21+ builtin `min`, module targets go1.24) removed from `phase4_final_validation_test.go` and `regression_test.go`.
- `phase4_final_validation_test.go`: `func adaptSessionCount(current, max int, load float64) int` named a parameter `max`, shadowing the package-level `max` — `return max(current/2, 1)` was calling an int as a function. Fixed by renaming the parameter to `maxSessions`.
- `phase4_final_validation_test.go`: `memoryDuration`/`diskDuration` were computed but their `t.Logf` usage lines had been dropped (found via diff review after a swarm-agent editing session got confused and cancelled after 40 min — see "Process note" below); restored both log lines rather than blank-assigning, since the original intent was clearly to log them.
- `phase5_production_validation_test.go`: two independent bugs — (1) `getRole Permissions(test.role)` at old line 772, a stray space breaking one identifier into two; the correctly-spelled `getRolePermissions` function already exists later in the file, so this was a pure typo, fixed by removing the space. (2) `import "math/rand"` was misplaced at the *end* of the file (line 1085, after other declarations — Go requires all imports at the top). Per repo convention (`go-rand-v2` rule), migrated to `math/rand/v2`: added to the top import block, all `rand.Intn(N)` call sites (5 of them) changed to `rand.IntN(N)`, and the `func init() { rand.Seed(...) }` block removed entirely since `v2` has no global `Seed` (auto-seeds since Go 1.20/1.22).
- `integration_test.go`: `for _, cloud := range clouds { ... }` never referenced `cloud` in the loop body — changed to `for range clouds`.

### Genuine API-mismatch bugs — files disabled (`.go` → `.go.disabled`), NOT fixed
These are real product-vs-test drift, not compile mechanics. Implementing them correctly requires product/domain decisions this session did not make:

1. **`backward_compat_final_test.go.disabled`** (~8 call sites) and **`production_readiness_test.go.disabled`** (~3 call sites): both call `hde.DecompressMemory(vmID, data)`. `*dwcp.HDE` (backend/core/network/dwcp/hde.go) has no such method — only `Decompress(data []byte) ([]byte, error)` exists, and per its own doc comment it does **not** reconstruct baselines/deltas per-VM the way these round-trip tests need. A correct `DecompressMemory` needs baseline-aware state tracking keyed by vmID that doesn't currently exist on `HDE`. Nontrivial; out of scope here.
2. **`performance_comparison_test.go.disabled`**: references `EnableLSTM` and `MaxVMs` fields on `dwcp.HDEConfig` — neither field exists on the real struct (verified against `hde.go:49-73`, full field list: LocalLevel, RegionalLevel, GlobalLevel, EnableDelta, BlockSize, MaxDeltaHistory, DeltaThreshold, EnableDictionary, DictSize, TrainingSamples, MaxMemoryUsage, CleanupInterval, EnableQuantization, QuantizationBits). Aspirational/wrong API, not a typo.

### Real test failures + a hang, discovered once the package finally compiled (separate from the above — these compile fine, they just don't pass)
Running `go test -run=. -bench=^$` (i.e. the actual `Test*` functions, not benchmarks) on this package for the first time ever surfaces:
- `TestPhase4_FinalIntegrationValidation/Phase2_ComponentValidation/HDE_Validation`: `assert.Greater(t, regionalRatio, 2.0, ...)` fails — actual ratio 1.90x vs required >2.0x. Real assertion against a real (simulated) compression pass, target not met.
- `TestPhase5_ProductionMonitoring/Metrics_Collection`: `assert.GreaterOrEqual(t, metricCount, 100, "Should collect 100+ metrics")` fails — actual count is 6.
- `TestPhase5_ProductionSimulation/Health_Monitoring_During_Rollout`: **hangs** — still running past a 50s timeout (uses `time.Sleep` patterns consistent with a "realistic production simulation" that was never tuned for fast test execution). This will hang any bare `go test ./...` on `backend/core` that doesn't scope away from this package.

None of this blocks `BenchmarkAMSTv1VsV3` or the other `Benchmark*` functions in `benchmark_test.go` — benchmarks run via `-run=^$ -bench=...` never execute the `Test*` functions, so novacron-38p's actual deliverable is unaffected. But **`go test ./...` on `backend/core` will now hang/fail where it silently skipped this package entirely before.** Recommend one of: (a) fix the assertions/timing with real product-owner input, (b) gate this package out of the default `go test ./...` invocation (build tag or separate CI step) until (a) happens, (c) re-disable specifically `phase5_production_validation_test.go`'s `TestPhase5_ProductionSimulation` (the hang) as a stopgap while leaving the rest enabled since they fail fast rather than hang.

## Process note (swarm-agent mishap, now fully resolved)
A `task`-tool subagent (ruflo-tracked, `agentId=agent-1783629382192-olevyl`) was dispatched to finish this compile sweep. It got lost in `find`/`cd` confusion between the real repo path and an unrelated, pre-existing git worktree at `.claude/worktrees/agent-a69d70d91d0dba4f2/` (a separate worktree on branch `worktree-agent-a69d70d91d0dba4f2`, someone else's in-progress work, left untouched), burned 40 minutes, and was cancelled by the harness. Along the way it accidentally left `phase5_production_validation_test.go` deleted from the real repo path (its `getRolePermissions` fix landed in the stale worktree copy instead). Recovered via `git checkout HEAD -- <path>` (file was still tracked at HEAD, zero data loss) and the fix was redone correctly in the actual repo path, verified with `git diff --stat` showing zero drift afterward. Flagging in case that worktree directory causes similar confusion for future agents/sessions — it's a known hazard in this repo layout.

## Verification
`CGO_ENABLED=1 go vet ./network/dwcp/v3/tests/...` and `go build` and `go test -c` all exit 0. `go test -run=^$ -bench=. -benchtime=1s` passes cleanly with real numbers (HDE compression up to 743 MB/s on 1MB payloads, real gzip/deflate-class compression ratios 1.1x-5.4x depending on data entropy, AMST metrics-update overhead ~700ns/op). Full numbers included in the novacron-38p update.

## References
novacron-38p (Phase 0 benchmarks / Go/No-Go decision) — this issue's debt was discovered while unblocking that work.

title: security/reputation_system.go: RecordByzantineBehavior self-deadlocks on quarantine (non-reentrant mutex locked twice)
description:
## Overview
Confirmed genuine, deterministic self-deadlock (not flaky) via novacron-3cd triage. `RecordByzantineBehavior` (reputation_system.go:264-286) does `rs.mu.Lock(); defer rs.mu.Unlock()` then calls `rs.checkQuarantine(rep)` while STILL holding the lock. `checkQuarantine` (line 456-465), when a node's reputation score drops to/below the quarantine threshold, calls `rs.QuarantineNode(...)` (line 463), which immediately does `rs.mu.Lock()` again (line 320) - a second Lock() call on a non-reentrant sync.RWMutex already held by the same goroutine. Permanent self-deadlock, confirmed via stack trace: goroutine blocked at reputation_system.go:320 inside QuarantineNode <- checkQuarantine:463 <- RecordByzantineBehavior:285.

Same pattern also present in RecordConsensusParticipation (241-260, checkQuarantine at 260) and RecordMessageSuccess/RecordMessageFailure (288-316, checkQuarantine at 300/315) - ANY of these four methods deadlocks the instant a node's score reaches the quarantine threshold with quarantine enabled.

## Impact
This hangs the entire calling goroutine (and, per the confirmed test hang, an entire test binary/process) the moment Byzantine behavior pushes any node to quarantine - i.e. exactly the security-critical scenario this system exists to handle. Not a theoretical edge case.

## Suggested fix
Split QuarantineNode into a lock-free internal variant (quarantineNodeLocked, no locking) called by checkQuarantine (already holding rs.mu), with the exported QuarantineNode wrapping it with Lock/Unlock for external callers.

## Evidence
backend/core/network/dwcp/v3/security package test suite hangs, confirmed via 'test timed out after 1m30s' with 90s timeout; full stack trace analysis in novacron-3cd triage.
close_reason: Fixed both non-reentrant self-deadlock paths in reputation_system.go: (1) checkQuarantine now calls a new lock-free quarantineNodeLocked instead of the public QuarantineNode (which re-locked rs.mu) - covers RecordByzantineBehavior/RecordConsensusParticipation/RecordMessageSuccess/RecordMessageFailure -> checkQuarantine; (2) cleanup now calls a new lock-free releaseQuarantineLocked instead of the public ReleaseQuarantine (same double-lock, in the background cleanup goroutine). Both public methods retained as locking wrappers; extractions are faithful (release still deletes the record - IsQuarantined/GetQuarantinedNodes read map membership as quarantine state). Added deterministic regression test TestReputationSystem_CleanupReleasesExpiredQuarantine (fails via 5s deadlock-timeout on pre-fix baseline, passes race-clean with fix). Full-file reentrant-lock sweep confirms these were the only two such paths. Verified: TestReputationSystem_QuarantineMechanism + new test pass; build+vet clean. Non-deadlock failures unmasked by removing the hang were filed separately: novacron-ffc (mode_security deadlock, P1), novacron-1h2 (MaxQuarantineCount gap, P2), novacron-e50 (impossible-assertion test bug, P3); byzantine_detector detection-logic failures + rs.config -race documented under novacron-3cd.

title: transport/multi_stream_tcp.go: RecordBytesSent never called - Prometheus metrics permanently report 0 bytes despite real traffic
description:
## Overview
MultiStreamTCP.Send()/sendChunk() (multi_stream_tcp.go:241-337) update internal atomic counters (m.totalBytesSent, stream.bytesSent) but never call m.metrics.RecordBytesSent(...) - the method that actually feeds MetricsCollector.GetMetrics()'s Prometheus-facing TotalBytesSent field. Contrast with rdma_transport.go:243,289, which correctly calls RecordBytesSent/RecordBytesReceived.

## Impact
Real, non-cosmetic observability bug: any dashboard/alerting built on MetricsCollector for the MultiStreamTCP transport always reports zero throughput regardless of actual traffic (confirmed: 1MB Send() succeeds via echo-server round-trip, but GetMetrics().TotalBytesSent reads 0).

## Evidence
backend/core/network/dwcp/transport, TestMetricsCollection. novacron-3cd triage.
close_reason: Fixed: MultiStreamTCP.Send now calls m.metrics.RecordBytesSent(len(data)) and Receive calls m.metrics.RecordBytesReceived(len(result)) - previously both only updated internal atomics that GetMetrics doesn't surface, so Prometheus TotalBytesSent/Recv always read 0. Matches rdma_transport.go. Fixes TestMetricsCollection; transport passes -race.

title: MigrationAdapter: vmBaselines map grows unbounded - full memory/disk copy per vmID, never evicted
description:
## Overview
adapter.vmBaselines (migration_adapter.go:29, map[string]*VMBaseline) stores a FULL COPY of every migrated VM's memory (VMBaseline.MemoryBaseline []byte) and disk blocks (DiskBaselines map[int][]byte) per unique vmID, via storeMemoryBaseline/storeDiskBaselines (lines ~583-610). Verified via direct grep: every reference to vmBaselines is either the write-path (check-then-store, existence checked only to avoid a redundant allocation, never to read baseline CONTENT for delta computation elsewhere) or a metrics count (baseline_count in GetMetrics, line 820). There is no delete() call anywhere in the file, and no code path reads a stored baseline's actual byte content for delta encoding or any other purpose.

## Impact
A long-running MigrationAdapter process that migrates N distinct VM IDs over its lifetime retains N full memory/disk snapshots in memory forever, unbounded. For any real deployment with VM churn (VMs migrated once and never again, or with rotating/ephemeral vmIDs), this is a genuine memory leak that will eventually exhaust available memory.

MaxMemoryUsage (MigrationAdapterConfig) does NOT bound this - it's used elsewhere as a per-payload receive-side size cap (readSizePrefixedPayload/readSizePrefixedDiskBlocks, the DoS-prevention fix from earlier in this session), not as a cap on vmBaselines map size or total retained baseline bytes.

## Suggested fix
Either (a) add an LRU/TTL eviction policy bounded by count or total bytes (using MaxMemoryUsage as the intended bound, now that it exists for a related purpose), or (b) if baselines are genuinely never read back (confirm this - the delta-encoding consumer this was presumably built for may not exist yet, matching the pattern of other aspirational/unwired code this session found), consider whether storing them at all serves any current purpose, versus deferring storage until an actual delta-encoding consumer exists.

## Evidence
Direct grep of every 'vmBaselines' reference in migration_adapter.go - write-only, no reads of content, no eviction, VMBaseline struct definition (line 165) confirms full []byte copies are held, not hashes/checksums.
